description:
FILED s524 (Fable, 2026-10-22) from the batch-6 merge probe b1-int-boundary line 10 (`18446744073709551615 == 18446744073709551616` perl eq / PCL ne).  SILENT WRONG, PRE-EXISTING: identical on the base 2534d7d0 and on s523b's tree; #2016 only made the shape reachable with two LITERALS (the right-hand literal is now perl's double).  A face of #1513's family (PCL has no 64-bit boundary and no NV precision loss), but a COMPARISON, which #1513's entry does not cover.

PROBE (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s513/review/p523b/ b1 line 10; the eight-line probe in the s524 PAUSE), perl 5.40.3 vs PCL (base = tree):
  18446744073709551615 == 1.8446744073709552e19     perl eq   PCL ne
  9007199254740993 == 9007199254740992.0            perl eq   PCL ne
  9007199254740993 == 9.007199254740993e15          perl eq   PCL ne
  18446744073709551615 <  1.8446744073709552e19     perl ge   PCL lt
  18446744073709551615 <=> 1.8446744073709552e19    perl 0    PCL -1
  (the same through variables)                      perl eq   PCL ne
  3 == 3.0                                          eq        eq
  9007199254740993 == 9007199254740993.0            perl eq   PCL ne   (the NV literal is already 2^53)

PERL'S RULE (pp_eq / pp_lt / pp_ncmp under PERL_PRESERVE_IVUV, sv.c SvIV_please): an operand that is an NV is compared AS AN INTEGER only when SvIV_please makes it IOK -- integral AND |nv| below 2**NV_PRESERVES_UV_BITS (53 on this box, so 2^53 itself is NOT preserved) -- otherwise BOTH sides are compared as NVs, i.e. the IV/UV side is CONVERTED TO A DOUBLE first and loses its low bits.  PCL's `p-==` / `p-<` / `p-<=>` hand an integer and a double to CL's `=` / `<`, which compare EXACTLY (rational comparison), so the two sides never meet where perl rounds them together.  #2450 implemented the same SvIV_please rule for `**` (an integral NV operand is an IV there) -- the predicate exists; the comparison family needs the OTHER half (an NV that is NOT IV-pleasable makes the comparison a double comparison).

FIX SHAPE (not designed): in the numeric-comparison entry (one helper, shared by == != < <= > >= <=>; grep for the existing integer/double fast arms), when one side is an integer and the other a double: if the double is integral and |d| < 2^53, compare exactly (as today -- that IS perl's integer compare); else coerce the integer to double-float first.  Cost: one typep + one comparison on the mixed path only; the integer-integer and double-double arms are untouched -- bench rows arith / useint / cfor must stay in the band.  Guard: a new file or `Pl/t/int-boundary-01.t` rows (the eight lines above, perl-probed); inverse-guard on the base.

NOT TO DO: do not touch the arithmetic family (`+ - *` beyond 64 bits stays exact, #1513 USER decision); do not key on the LITERAL (a variable holding the double behaves the same).

Impact: low in ordinary programs (needs an integer above 2^53 next to a double); the 64bitint / numconvert families are already registered under #1513.
subject: DIVERGENCE (numeric comparison, #1513 face): an INTEGER compared with a DOUBLE is exact in PCL where perl converts the integer to NV unless the NV is integral below 2^53 -- 9007199254740993 == 9007199254740992.0 is eq in perl, ne in PCL (pre-existing; exposed by the #2016 merge probe)
